title: Debt interest of Tk 1.27 lakh crore leaves less for social spending
excerpt: Bangladesh's first debt conference opens in Cox's Bazar as foreign loan repayments hit a record $4.49 billion and new commitments fall to a 14-year low.

image.alt: Beach umbrellas under a stormy sky at Kolatoli Point, Cox's Bazar
image.credit: Tanvir Rahat / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
The Finance Division and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) are holding Bangladesh's first international debt conference in Cox's Bazar on 15 and 16 November, as interest payments take a growing share of the budget, The Business Standard reported. Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury is due to open it.

Key figures

  • Total government debt: Tk 22.06 lakh crore, of which Tk 9.59 lakh crore is foreign debt, as the finance minister told Parliament on 12 July.
  • Interest this year: Tk 1,27,500 crore budgeted for FY27 (fiscal year 2026-27): Tk 1,05,000 crore on domestic debt and Tk 22,500 crore on foreign debt.
  • Foreign repayments: a record $4.494 billion in FY26 ($2.95 billion principal, $1.54 billion interest), according to Economic Relations Division (ERD) data.
  • New foreign loans: commitments of $5.243 billion in FY26, the lowest in 14 years.
  • Risk rating: the IMF's 2025 debt sustainability analysis put Bangladesh at moderate risk of debt distress.

The newspaper, citing a Finance Division report, said rising interest costs leave less money for education, healthcare, social protection and development projects. The government plans an annual borrowing plan this fiscal year and a separate Debt Management Office, and is looking at sukuk, green, blue and SDG-linked bonds. The UN General Assembly extended Bangladesh's preparation for leaving the least developed country (LDC) group by three years, to November 2029, which delays the loss of some cheap loans.

Why it matters

Interest is budgeted at Tk 1.27 lakh crore this year, at a time when foreign grants to NGOs are also shrinking. If the state has less room to spend on health, education and safety nets, more pressure falls on NGO services. Groups working on budgets and social protection may want to follow the conference outcomes and the planned borrowing plan.

What to watch

Any announcements at the close of the conference on 16 November, the first Annual Borrowing Plan, and the revised FY27 budget.

Sources
